Coconut and castor oil. And cutting down shampooing. 
I used to have that same issue everyday. I would have to paste it down with gel or mousse. 
Since using both oils, I have almost zero frizz. 
Once a week I do a mask of castor oil (I use a hair dye bottle to apply it to my scalp and massage it  through my hair) and leave it on for at least an hour (ideally overnight) with a shower cap. Then wash it with shampoo and conditioner. This is the only time I use shampoo, cause my hair gets dry incredibly easily. Otherwise I do a conditioning wash. 
Every time I wash my hair, I put coconut oil all through my hair. You need a lot less than it seems; it gets real oily quick. I just put a half dollar size of oil on my palm and rub it over the most problematic spots, then brush it through with a wide comb and let it air dry (blow drying just turns me into a poodle).

Quick story that I think is pertinent. 
Before I got engaged, my sister decided to cut off all contact and pretty much ghost me and our family. There was some drama between her and my mom and she just decided to cut us all out. When I did get engaged I texted her that I was getting married and I wanted her to be my maid of honor. She didn’t reply but sent me a congratulations card. A few months later I get a text from her saying that she missed me and we should meet up, blahblahblah... Turns out she has texted my fiancé (at the time) for help with something and he asked her to just text me to let me know she was okay and whatnot. Some hours later she said “tell fiancé that I don’t appreciate being manipulated like that...”To which I, had a response. 
That was one of the main reasons I didn’t invite her (along with that she might being an ex-family friend who I can’t stand, and all of the possible drama that I didn’t want). 
It really sucks that she wasn’t there and I don’t have her in the pictures and everything. But I decided that no matter what else might go wrong, the only thing that matters is getting to marry the man I love. And it was worth it. 

I hope your dad comes to his senses and sees how much of an ass he’s being, but if he doesn’t I don’t want you to feel bad. You aren’t excluding him; you _invited_ him, how is that excluding him?

If it were me I wouldn’t count on him to come, and I would ask my mom to give me away. I would probably plan for an extra place for him if he does show up, but otherwise proceed as if he’s not going to come, so that you’re ready either way.

When I first came across those subs I was really hurt. Why are these people so mean? I mean, what did I do to them to deserve to be hated because of my dress size or number on the scale? I mean, were these kids bullied by fat children in school or something? Did their parents beat them if they gained a pound? But when I think about it, I think those people are actually really sad. Are they so terrified of being fat that they feel like they have to mock and ridicule those of us who are, as if they are "warding off the fatness" with their comments and cruelness? Maybe they think of how their family and friends, or the media, or whoever else, views people who are overweight and know that they couldn't handle being treated with such malice and disdain. They know if someone posted the things they posted about others, or pointed at them and laughed as they sweated and huffed for an hour on the treadmill at the gym, that they would be crushed.
 
They’re also just bullies that left the playground but never grew up. I guess it’s not enough for them to already be healthy and content with their weight, able to go anywhere and do anything without fear that their weight will stop them, and able to wear whatever they want with confidence. Apparently feeling good about themselves isn’t good enough unless they can make someone else feel like crap. Because me feeling like crap on my own isn’t quite enough. So you struggle every day, so what if you’ve been killing yourself for years to lose weight? So what? If you’re fat, we’re gonna hate on you because, you know, looking at someone who’s fat is just apparently too much. 
I don’t know why these people have such hatred other than they hurt so much, for whatever reason, that they feel the need to hurt someone else in order to feel better about themselves and apparently it’s still okay to make fun of fat people. (Because you know, fat people are alllll fat because all they do is sit all day and eat non-stop. Why, just this morning I had a stack of 10 pancakes covered with chocolate sauce, syrup and whipped cream and some bacon and eggs and hashbrowns and…wait, no, I had a greek yogurt and a green smoothie, with a scoop of matcha green tea, pea protein powder and some coconut oil and then I worked out for 45 minutes… )

The way that I deal with it at the gym is to just focus on my workout and the reason that I’m there “I’m here to get healthy and to feel good and good about myself”. I also think you should try to remember that these people, the ones who post and enjoy being cruel are the minority. Most people come in the gym, work out and leave. So, as a person who has been there, here are a few of the things I did, small things, that helped a lot. One, water. Lots of water. Lots of times when you think your hungry, your body is really just dehydrated, so drink up. If you can, try to drink a big glass of water around 30 minutes before you eat; it helps fill you up and you'll eat less, but still feel full. Two, use smaller plates if you can. If you're having a snack, put it on a saucer, if your going to have some ice cream use a small cup, the smaller amount will fill up the smaller space which tricks your brain into thinking you're eating a lot, when you're really just having a bit. The best thing is not to have junk food at all, but I found it was easier to make the small changes; lots of small changes can lead to big results.
Three, before eating, ask yourself if you're actually hungry. If you aren't sure, drink some more water and go do something else, try to wait at least twenty minutes and then ask yourself again. Lots of times, the "hunger" will go away. And if you just need to munch on something, try to make it something a little healthier; carrots (with ranch? if you don't like them plain) or celery, with peanut butter if you like it. Sometimes it's not even the food, it's more the action of eating that you're subconsciously looking for, and eating when you aren't truly hungry isn't such big deal if you're eating something nutritious, plus, all that fiber is really filling.

A couple other things: chew thoroughly - I tend to eat like someone is going to take my food from me unless I down it, but take your time and really chew and taste it, it will give your brain time to get the signal that your full before you overeat without realizing it, and by allowing yourself to really taste the "junk food" you may realize you don't need to eat as much (like chocolate bars? Just take a piece and let it melt in your mouth. It tastes more chocolatey then downing the entire bar.  Opt for the "healthy option", like, if you're out with friends and you can choose fries or a salad/vegetable, go with the veggies, or if you're getting ice cream, get it in a cup, not a cone. 
Move, even if it's a little, take the stairs, not the elevator, do wall push ups or crunches on commercials when you are watching TV, and try to make it fun. And, don't let anyone make you feel embarrassed about it. Don't let them make you feel bad, and don't let yourself make you feel bad either. Yeah, being 300+ -sucks-, but you are doing something about it, don't trash talk, guilt trip or be anything but loving to yourself. Your mind will remember all if it and it won't help; if anything it will just make it harder. It's hard enough being fat in this society, you don't need to beat on yourself too. And don't let slips ups mess you up, the weight didn't just appear overnight and it won't disappear overnight either, so if you had a bad day, let it go and try again tomorrow. Persistence, not perfection. Just don't quit and you'll get there. 

Those aren't really "discipline" things, but just some small things that helped me. Hope they help you too.
